content_preview.title: JetBrains Patches Critical Hub Authentication Bypass and Account Takeover Flaws Across Its IDE Ecosystem
content_preview.summary: JetBrains patched three critical Hub and YouTrack flaws enabling account takeover and authentication bypass, alongside code-execution fixes across IntelliJ, GoLand, and TeamCity.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

On July 2, 2026, JetBrains disclosed patches for three critical vulnerabilities in its Hub and YouTrack products that could let attackers take over administrator accounts or bypass standard sign-in controls, according to [GBHackers](https://gbhackers.com/jetbrains-patches-critical-hub-authentication-bypass/) and [Cyber Press](https://cyberpress.org/jetbrains-patches-authentication-bypass-code-execution/). In an advisory published to its own blog, JetBrains said the flaws were discov...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured News piece with an Overview / What We Know / Beyond the Identity Layer / What We Don't Know / Analysis flow. Appropriate technical depth for a patch advisory. Correctly separates vendor-attributed facts from single-outlet specifics, and explicitly flags what JetBrains did not disclose (per-IDE CVSS scores, how long deployments were vulnerable).
editor_notes.source_verification: Four sources. source-0.html.gz (blog.jetbrains.com) READ from disk — CONFIRMS: May 2026 discovery ('In May 2026, independent researchers and the JetBrains team together identified several critical vulnerabilities'), 'advanced security research that leveraged AI-assisted testing techniques', 'no evidence that any of these vulnerabilities were exploited outside of testing environments', CVE-2026-56141 = admin account takeover via authentication token forgery (Cloud + Server), CVE-2026-56142 = email verification bypass, CVE-2026-50242 = admin takeover via direct database access (Server only), Hub 2026.1.13757 plus backports 2025.3.148033 / 2025.2.148048 / 2025.1.148120 / 2024.3.148430 / 2024.2.148429, versions earlier than 2024.2 unpatched, YouTrack Cloud already patched. source-3.html.gz (cybersecuritynews.com, archive.org fallback, status 200) READ from disk — CONFIRMS the code-execution vectors (Kotlin unsafe deserialization in build cache metadata, GoLand RCE via untrusted project configuration, IntelliJ filename-completion command injection and guest-user command execution, TeamCity RCE via Perforce connection settings) and the remediation guidance (prioritize upgrading Hub/YouTrack, credential/token rotation, access-control review); HOWEVER the five vector phrases the article places inside quotation marks are NOT verbatim in the snapshot (0 exact matches) — they are the Herald's reformatted labels of the outlet's prose. source-1 gbhackers.com and source-2 cyberpress.org snapshots FAILED (HTTP 403, file null); as a last resort both live URLs were WebFetched for verification. GBHackers CONFIRMS: Hub as 'the central identity and access management component that authenticates users for products such as YouTrack, TeamCity, and other JetBrains services', restore codes with 'insufficient randomness', 'predict or brute-force restore codes to hijack accounts', CWE-338/CWE-915/CWE-306 mapped to the three CVEs, all backport versions, and a July 2, 2026 publication date. Cyber Press CONFIRMS the single-outlet specifics: CVSS 9.8 for CVE-2026-56141, CVE-2026-56142 as privilege escalation, CVE-2026-53915 (GoLand RCE from untrusted project config), CVE-2026-49373 (TeamCity Perforce command-injection RCE) — none overstated.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: CVE IDs, CVSS 9.8, CWE mappings, affected products, patched/backport versions, and the July 2, 2026 disclosure date all trace correctly to the cited sources. Single-outlet specifics (CVSS 9.8, CVE-2026-53915, CVE-2026-49373) are correctly attributed to Cyber Press alone and each is genuinely present in that outlet. Two quote-fidelity issues (below) are the only defects and are recoverable via corrections.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. No sensationalism, no exploit walkthroughs or step-by-step attack mechanics, no editorializing. Remediation framed as vendor/outlet guidance.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. The only prior 2026 JetBrains security article (2026-06/18, fifteen malicious JetBrains Marketplace plugins stealing AI API keys) covers a distinct event — malicious third-party plugins, not vendor-patched Hub/YouTrack authentication flaws. Distinct CVEs, distinct products, distinct story.
concerns: The article places five IDE code-execution vector descriptions ('Filename completion command injection in IntelliJ IDEA', 'Guest user account command execution in IntelliJ IDEA', 'Untrusted project configuration in GoLand', 'Perforce connection settings RCE in TeamCity', 'Unsafe deserialization in Kotlin build cache metadata') inside quotation marks attributed to Cyber Security News, but none appear verbatim in that outlet's snapshot; they are accurate reformattings of the source's prose rather than direct quotes.

The GBHackers description of Hub is quoted as 'identity and access management component for YouTrack, TeamCity, and other JetBrains services'; the outlet's actual wording is 'the central identity and access management component that authenticates users for products such as YouTrack, TeamCity, and other JetBrains services' — the quotation compresses the phrase without an ellipsis.

Two sources (gbhackers.com, cyberpress.org) bot-blocked the archiver (HTTP 403), so their snapshots are null; content was verified via last-resort live WebFetch. cyberpress.org is off the source allowlist — a normal editorial warning, not disqualifying.
recommendations: Both quote-fidelity issues are documented in an accompanying corrections record so readers see the exact wording of each source.
No action needed on the CVE, CVSS, version, or date specifics — all verified accurate against the cited outlets.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, neutral, well-sourced News report on a publicly disclosed JetBrains patch. All CVE IDs, the CVSS 9.8 score, CWE mappings, affected products, patch/backport versions, and the disclosure date verify against the cited sources; single-outlet specifics are correctly attributed and not overstated; the piece is distinct from prior JetBrains coverage. The only defects are two minor quote-fidelity slips (reformatted phrasing inside quotation marks), which are honestly summarizable in a corrections note. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
